stem: A 64-year-old on chemotherapy has fever 38.6°C and neutrophils 0.2 ×10⁹/L. He is haemodynamically stable and no source is found initially.
ask: What is the MOST APPROPRIATE initial management?
options: Admit for observation and begin antibiotics only if another fever is recorded.
Start oral amoxicillin–clavulanate and arrange urgent oncology follow-up.
Give IV ceftriaxone alone after cultures and review treatment tomorrow.
Give IV vancomycin alone while investigating a possible line infection.
Obtain cultures promptly and start urgent IV antipseudomonal antibiotics.
explanations: Admission and cultures are sensible but are not sufficient: fever with marked chemotherapy-associated neutropenia needs prompt empiric antibiotics even while vital signs are stable.
Outpatient oral treatment is only for appropriately assessed low-risk patients on an established pathway; oral amoxicillin–clavulanate alone does not provide adequate empiric antipseudomonal cover.
Ceftriaxone alone does not reliably cover Pseudomonas. In high-risk febrile neutropenia, use a recommended antipseudomonal regimen rather than a narrow substitute.
Vancomycin targets Gram-positive pathogens and cannot replace the necessary Gram-negative antipseudomonal cover. Add specific Gram-positive cover only when justified.
Obtain blood cultures without delaying treatment, give prompt empiric IV antipseudomonal antibiotics as guided by local policy, and continue monitoring and source investigation.
pearl: Neutropenic fever: do not wait for hypotension; early broad-spectrum antipseudomonal IV therapy saves lives.
pivot: If formally assessed low risk after initial treatment, use a supervised outpatient antibiotic pathway with planned review; otherwise continue inpatient IV therapy.

stem: A 58-year-old with bipolar disorder, stable on lithium for years, starts hydrochlorothiazide. One week later he has vomiting, coarse tremor, dysarthria and ataxia. Creatinine is mildly increased.
ask: Which is the MOST LIKELY mechanism?

Thiazides enhance renal lithium excretion causing withdrawal
The new drug directly produces serotonin syndrome
Hydrochlorothiazide causes a complete AV block in all patients
Thiazide-associated sodium loss increases renal lithium reabsorption, causing toxicity
explanations: There is no inactivation reaction.
Thiazides typically reduce lithium clearance, not increase it.
Clonus/hyperreflexia and serotonergic exposure are not described.

pivot: If he had fine tremor with normal lithium level and no ataxia, a benign dose-related side effect could be considered.

Atrial flutter with a fixed 2:1 block

stem: A 26-year-old at 9 weeks gestation has unilateral lower abdominal pain and light bleeding. Ultrasound demonstrates an empty uterus and a 3-cm adnexal mass; serum β-hCG is 3800 IU/L.
ask: Which diagnosis is MOST LIKELY?
options: Cervical insufficiency causing painless mid-trimester cervical opening.
Ovarian hyperstimulation after recent assisted reproductive treatment.
Placenta praevia causing late-pregnancy painless vaginal bleeding.
Threatened intrauterine miscarriage confirmed by a gestational sac.
Tubal ectopic pregnancy with an adnexal mass and empty uterus.
explanations: Cervical insufficiency typically causes painless shortening or dilatation in the mid-trimester; it does not explain a 9-week pregnancy with an extrauterine mass.
Ovarian hyperstimulation is considered following fertility stimulation, often with bilaterally enlarged multicystic ovaries and ascites, rather than an isolated 3-cm adnexal gestational mass.
Placenta praevia is a cause of antepartum bleeding later in gestation and cannot explain this first-trimester ultrasound pattern.
A threatened miscarriage refers to bleeding with a known intrauterine gestation and closed cervix. No intrauterine sac is visible while an adnexal mass is present.

A positive pregnancy test, empty uterus and adnexal mass make a tubal ectopic most likely. Her haemodynamic status and other ultrasound details determine whether expectant, methotrexate or surgical management is appropriate.
pearl: A positive pregnancy test with pain/bleeding is ectopic until excluded, even without shock.
pivot: If unstable with peritonism/free fluid, immediate resuscitation and surgical treatment supersede serial β-hCG surveillance.

pivot: Clinical chorioamnionitis, fetal compromise or significant abruption changes the balance towards delivery.
